## `std::enumerable`

- `trait Enumerable<T>` - Enumerable methods of a sequence of `T`.
  - `fn group_by(self, key: fn(T) -> K) -> Map<K, List<T>>` - Groups the elements by key, keeping their order within each group.
  - `fn count_by(self, key: fn(T) -> K) -> Map<K, int>` - Counts the elements per key.
  - `fn tally(self) -> Map<T, int>` - Counts each distinct element (alias: `frequencies`).
  - `fn frequencies(self) -> Map<T, int>` - Same as `tally`.
  - `fn sum_by(self, f: fn(T) -> N) -> N` - Sum of `f(x)` over the elements.
  - `fn unique(self) -> List<T>` - The first occurrence of each distinct element, in order.
  - `fn unique_by(self, key: fn(T) -> K) -> List<T>` - The first element of each distinct key, in order.
  - `fn chunk_by(self, key: fn(T) -> K) -> List<List<T>>` - Maximal runs of consecutive elements with equal keys.
  - `fn each_slice(self, n: int) -> List<List<T>>` - Lists of `n` elements (the last may be shorter); panics when `n` is 0.
  - `fn partition_by(self, pred: fn(T) -> bool) -> (List<T>, List<T>)` - `(matching, rest)`, each in order.
  - `fn intersperse(self, sep: T) -> List<T>` - `sep` between consecutive elements.
  - `fn zip_with(self, other: List<U>, f: fn(T, U) -> R) -> List<R>` - `[f(x0, y0), f(x1, y1), ..]` up to the shorter length.
  - `fn index_of(self, x: T) -> Option<int>` - Index of the first element equal to `x`.
  - `fn sorted(self) -> List<T>` - A sorted copy.
  - `fn sorted_by_key(self, key: fn(T) -> K) -> List<T>` - A copy sorted by key (stable).
  - `fn sorted_by_key_desc(self, key: fn(T) -> K) -> List<T>` - A copy sorted by key, largest first (stable).
  - `fn sort_by_key_desc(self, key: fn(T) -> K)` - Sorts in place by key, largest first (stable).
  - `fn to_list(self) -> List<T>` - The elements as a list.
